---
title: "Sentiment Analysis using the NRC Lexicon: Finn the Wolfhound"
output: html_document
---


### Use this as a starter file for sentiment analysis.  You should try each of the three lexicons. 
### It may make sense to copy this file and use one file per lexicon.
```{r}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidytext)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)


load(here("data/finn_clean.rda"))
```
### im assining values to each word 

```{r}
nrc <- get_sentiments("nrc")

nrc |> inner_join(finn_clean, by = "word", multiple = "all",
                  relationship = "many-to-many") -> fw_nrc
```
```{r}
fw_nrc |> 
  group_by(sentiment) |> 
  summarize(number = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(number))
``` 

###from the word sentiment it looks to me that it is a neutralbook with fear being a top word. 
```{r}
fw_nrc |> 
  filter(sentiment == "fear") |> 
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |> 
  head(20) |> 
  kable(caption = "Top 20 'FEAR' words in Finn the Wolfhound")
```
### looking at the words it does help pain a picture of the book but i will also looko at the trusting words
```{r}
fw_nrc |> 
  filter(sentiment == "trust") |> 
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |> 
  head(20) |> 
  kable(caption = "Top 20 'Trust' words in Finn the Wolfhound")
```
